source.text: אֵ֜לֶּה מַסְעֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָצְא֛וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: These [are the] journeyings of [the] sons of Israel who went out from [the] land of Egypt by their armies, by [the] hand of Moses and Aaron.

en.L: These [are] the journeys of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, who went out from the land of Egypt by their armies, under the hand of Moses and Aaron.
en.B: These are the stages of the journey of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} when they came out of the land of Egypt by their divisions, led by Moses and Aaron.
en.R: This is the list of the places where the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} stopped on their journey after they came out of Egypt in their troops. Moses and Aaron led them.

es.L: Estas [son] las jornadas de los hijos de Israel, que salieron de la tierra de Egipto según sus ejércitos, bajo la mano de Moisés y Aarón.
es.B: Estas son las etapas del viaje de los israelitas cuando salieron de la tierra de Egipto por escuadrones, guiados por Moisés y Aarón.
es.R: Esta es la lista de los lugares donde los israelitas se detuvieron en su viaje después de salir de Egipto en grupos ordenados. Moisés y Aarón los guiaban.

fr.L: Voici les déplacements des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, qui sortirent du pays d’Égypte selon leurs armées, sous la main de Moïse et d’Aaron.
fr.B: Voici les étapes du voyage des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} lorsqu’ils sortirent du pays d’Égypte par troupes, sous la conduite de Moïse et d’Aaron.
fr.R: Voici la liste des endroits où les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} se sont arrêtés pendant leur voyage, après être sortis d’Égypte en troupes organisées. Moïse et Aaron les conduisaient.

sw.L: Hizi [ndizo] safari za wana wa Israeli, waliotoka katika nchi ya Misri kwa majeshi yao, chini ya mkono wa Musa na Haruni.
sw.B: Hizi ndizo hatua za safari ya Waisraeli walipotoka katika nchi ya Misri kwa vikosi vyao, wakiongozwa na Musa na Haruni.
sw.R: Hii ndiyo orodha ya mahali ambapo Waisraeli walisimama katika safari yao baada ya kutoka Misri kwa vikosi vyao. Musa na Haruni waliwaongoza.

decisions.choice: journeys: the stages of the march, from one camp to the next
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "set out", which is repeated in every line of the list that follows (verses 5-49). Each "journey" is one move from a camp to the next, as in 10:12 ("by their stages"). The chapter looks back over the whole route from Egypt to the plains of Moab.

decisions.choice: by their armies: in ordered companies, like a marching army
decisions.reason: The word means a host or army. Israel left Egypt organized as a people under arms (Exodus 12:41, 51), and the tribes marched in their units (chapter 2; 10:14-28).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses and Aaron: under their leadership
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" someone means through or under that person. Moses and Aaron led the people out at God's command.

decisions.choice: the stages of the journey (Balanced); the list of the places where they stopped (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the plural "journeys" means: one journey made in many stages. Literal keeps "journeys".

decisions.choice: armies (Literal); divisions (Balanced); troops (Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Numbers for this word (10:14): each level uses its usual term for the army's units.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("sortirent", "partirent", "campèrent"); passé composé at Readable ("sont sortis", "ont quitté", "ont campé")
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the French narrative: the written narrative past at Literal and Balanced, the spoken past at Readable.

source.text: וַיִּכְתֹּ֨ב מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־מוֹצָאֵיהֶ֛ם לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֥לֶּה מַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם לְמוֹצָאֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And wrote Moses their startings out by their journeyings at [the] mouth of Yahweh; and these [are] their journeyings by their startings out.

en.L: And Moses wrote down their starting places by their journeys at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and these [are] their journeys by their starting places.
en.B: Moses wrote down the places they set out from, stage by stage, at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command. These are their journeys, listed by their starting points.
en.R: At {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command, Moses wrote down the places where each part of their journey began. Here is the list of their journeys, place by place.

es.L: Y escribió Moisés sus puntos de partida según sus jornadas, por boca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; y estas [son] sus jornadas según sus puntos de partida.
es.B: Moisés anotó los lugares de donde partieron, etapa por etapa, por orden {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Estas son sus jornadas, según sus puntos de partida.
es.R: Por orden {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, Moisés escribió los lugares donde comenzó cada parte de su viaje. Esta es la lista de sus jornadas, lugar por lugar.

fr.L: Et Moïse écrivit leurs points de départ selon leurs déplacements, selon la bouche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; et voici leurs déplacements selon leurs points de départ.
fr.B: Moïse mit par écrit les lieux d’où ils partirent, étape par étape, sur l’ordre {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Voici leurs étapes, selon leurs points de départ.
fr.R: Sur l’ordre {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, Moïse a écrit le nom des lieux où chaque partie de leur voyage a commencé. Voici la liste de leurs étapes, lieu après lieu.

sw.L: Naye Musa akaandika mahali pao pa kuanzia kwa safari zao, kwa kinywa cha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; na hizi [ndizo] safari zao kwa mahali pao pa kuanzia.
sw.B: Musa aliandika mahali walipoanzia safari, hatua kwa hatua, kwa amri ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Hizi ndizo safari zao, kufuatana na mahali walipoanzia.
sw.R: Kwa amri ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Musa aliandika majina ya mahali ambapo kila sehemu ya safari yao ilianzia. Hii ndiyo orodha ya safari zao, mahali kwa mahali.

decisions.choice: at the mouth of Yahweh: Moses wrote the list at the LORD's command
decisions.reason: The phrase stands after "Moses wrote" and most naturally says that the writing itself was commanded, as other records were (Exodus 17:14; 34:27). It could also be read with "their journeys": the people moved from camp to camp at the LORD's command, as 9:18-23 says with the same phrase. Both are true of the journey; the question is only which the phrase points to here.

decisions.choice: their starting places: the places from which each stage began
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "go out" and names a point of departure. Each line of the list names a place left and a place reached.

decisions.choice: the two halves reverse the order of the two nouns
decisions.reason: The verse says "starting places by journeys" and then "journeys by starting places". The crossing pattern rounds off the heading: what follows is a full record of the route, stage by stage.

decisions.choice: the places they set out from ... starting points
decisions.reason: Balanced uses two different expressions for the one Hebrew word so that the reversed order still reads naturally. Literal keeps "starting places" both times.

source.text: וַיִּסְע֤וּ מֵֽרַעְמְסֵס֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן מִֽמָּחֳרַ֣ת הַפֶּ֗סַח יָצְא֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּיָ֣ד רָמָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out from Rameses in the month the first, on [the] fifteenth day of the month the first; from [the] next day of the Passover went out [the] sons of Israel with a hand raised before [the] eyes of all Egypt,

en.L: And they set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the day after the Passover the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went out with a raised hand before the eyes of all Egypt,
en.B: They set out from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} marched out boldly in full view of all the Egyptians,
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after the Passover. They marched out boldly, and all the Egyptians saw them go.

es.L: Y partieron de Ramsés en el mes primero, el día quince del mes primero; el día siguiente a la Pascua salieron los hijos de Israel con mano alzada a los ojos de todo Egipto,
es.B: Partieron de Ramsés el día quince del primer mes. Al día siguiente de la Pascua, los israelitas salieron con valentía a la vista de todos los egipcios,
es.R: Los israelitas salieron de Ramsés el día quince del primer mes, el día después de la Pascua. Se marcharon con valor, y todos los egipcios los vieron irse.

fr.L: Et ils partirent de Ramsès au premier mois, le quinzième jour du premier mois ; le lendemain de la Pâque, les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël sortirent la main levée, sous les yeux de toute l’Égypte,
fr.B: Ils partirent de Ramsès le quinzième jour du premier mois. Le lendemain de la Pâque, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} sortirent avec assurance, à la vue de tous les Égyptiens,
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont quitté Ramsès le quinzième jour du premier mois, le lendemain de la Pâque. Ils sont sortis la tête haute, et tous les Égyptiens les ont vus partir.

sw.L: Nao wakasafiri kutoka Ramesesi katika mwezi wa kwanza, siku ya kumi na tano ya mwezi wa kwanza; kesho yake baada ya Pasaka wana wa Israeli wakatoka kwa mkono ulioinuliwa mbele ya macho ya Misri yote,
sw.B: Walisafiri kutoka Ramesesi siku ya kumi na tano ya mwezi wa kwanza. Siku iliyofuata Pasaka, Waisraeli walitoka kwa ujasiri, Wamisri wote wakiwaona,
sw.R: Waisraeli waliondoka Ramesesi siku ya kumi na tano ya mwezi wa kwanza, siku moja baada ya Pasaka. Walitoka kwa ujasiri, na Wamisri wote waliwaona wakienda.

decisions.choice: the fifteenth of the first month, the day after the Passover
decisions.reason: The Passover lamb was killed on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month (Exodus 12:6, 18; Numbers 28:16). The firstborn of Egypt died that night, and Israel left the next day (Exodus 12:29-34, 51).

decisions.choice: with a raised hand: openly and boldly
decisions.reason: A raised hand is a sign of strength and confidence. Israel did not slip away as runaways but left in the open, as Exodus 14:8 also says.

decisions.choice: Rameses: a city in the eastern Nile Delta
decisions.reason: Rameses was one of the store cities that Israel had been forced to build (Exodus 1:11), and the first point of departure in Exodus 12:37.

decisions.choice: all the Egyptians
decisions.reason: "All Egypt" means the people of Egypt, who saw Israel go. Literal keeps "all Egypt".

decisions.choice: ends with a comma
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on into verse 4, which tells what the Egyptians were doing as Israel left. Readable closes the sentence here.

source.text: וּמִצְרַ֣יִם מְקַבְּרִ֗ים אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בָּהֶ֖ם כָּל־בְּכ֑וֹר וּבֵאלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם עָשָׂ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה שְׁפָטִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: and Egypt [were] burying those whom had struck Yahweh among them, every firstborn; and on their gods had done Yahweh judgments.

en.L: and the Egyptians [were] burying those whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck down among them, every firstborn; and on their gods {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had carried out judgments.
en.B: while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck down among them. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had also carried out judgments on their gods.
en.R: At that time the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck dead. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had also brought judgment on their gods.

es.L: y los egipcios [estaban] enterrando a los que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había herido entre ellos, a todo primogénito; y sobre sus dioses {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había ejecutado juicios.
es.B: mientras los egipcios enterraban a todos sus primogénitos, a quienes {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había herido de muerte entre ellos. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} también había ejecutado juicios contra sus dioses.
es.R: En ese momento los egipcios estaban enterrando a todos sus primogénitos, a quienes {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había hecho morir. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} también había hecho caer su juicio sobre sus dioses.

fr.L: et les Égyptiens enterraient ceux que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait frappés parmi eux, tout premier-né ; et sur leurs dieux {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait exercé des jugements.
fr.B: pendant que les Égyptiens enterraient tous leurs premiers-nés, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait frappés parmi eux. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait aussi exercé ses jugements sur leurs dieux.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, les Égyptiens enterraient tous leurs premiers-nés, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait fait mourir. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait aussi fait tomber son jugement sur leurs dieux.

sw.L: nao Wamisri walikuwa wakiwazika wale ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapiga miongoni mwao, kila mzaliwa wa kwanza; na juu ya miungu yao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa ametekeleza hukumu.
sw.B: wakati Wamisri walipokuwa wakiwazika wazaliwa wao wote wa kwanza, ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amewapiga miongoni mwao. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa ametekeleza hukumu pia juu ya miungu yao.
sw.R: Wakati huo Wamisri walikuwa wakiwazika wazaliwa wao wote wa kwanza, ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amewaua. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa ameihukumu pia miungu yao.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians were burying: what was going on as Israel left
decisions.reason: The verb form describes an action in progress. While Israel marched out boldly, the Egyptians were busy with their dead. The contrast shows who had been defeated.

decisions.choice: judgments on their gods: the LORD showed the gods of Egypt to be powerless
decisions.reason: The LORD had said he would carry out judgments on all the gods of Egypt (Exodus 12:12). The gods could not protect their people, even the firstborn of the royal house (Exodus 12:29).

decisions.choice: while ... / At that time
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the clause to the end of verse 3 with "while"; Readable, which ended verse 3 with a full stop, begins a new sentence.

source.text: וַיִּסְע֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵרַעְמְסֵ֑ס וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּסֻכֹּֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And set out [the] sons of Israel from Rameses and camped at Succoth.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left Rameses and camped at Succoth.

es.L: Y partieron los hijos de Israel de Ramsés y acamparon en Sucot.
es.B: Los israelitas partieron de Ramsés y acamparon en Sucot.
es.R: Los israelitas salieron de Ramsés y acamparon en Sucot.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël partirent de Ramsès et campèrent à Souccoth.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} partirent de Ramsès et campèrent à Souccoth.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont quitté Ramsès et ont campé à Souccoth.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakasafiri kutoka Ramesesi, wakapiga kambi Sukothi.
sw.B: Waisraeli walisafiri kutoka Ramesesi, wakapiga kambi Sukothi.
sw.R: Waisraeli waliondoka Ramesesi, wakapiga kambi Sukothi.

decisions.choice: set out ... and camped: one stage of the march
decisions.reason: From here to verse 49 each line has the same two verbs: they pulled up their tents at one place and pitched them at the next. The repeated form makes the list a record of the whole route, stage after stage.

decisions.choice: Succoth: the first stop after Rameses
decisions.reason: Succoth, "booths", was the first camp on the way out of Egypt (Exodus 12:37; 13:20). Its site is not known for certain.

decisions.choice: set out ... camped (Literal, Balanced); left ... camped (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps one fixed wording for every line of the list (verses 5-49), so that the reader hears the repetition of the Hebrew. Readable says "left", as in 21:11.

decisions.choice: partieron de ... y acamparon en (Literal, Balanced); salieron de ... y acamparon en (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps one fixed wording for every line of the list (verses 5-49), so that the reader hears the repetition of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: partirent de ... et campèrent à (Literal, Balanced); ont quitté ... et ont campé à (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps one fixed wording for every line of the list (verses 5-49), so that the reader hears the repetition of the Hebrew, as 21:10-11 do.

decisions.choice: wakasafiri kutoka ..., wakapiga kambi (Literal); walisafiri kutoka ..., wakapiga kambi (Balanced); waliondoka ..., wakapiga kambi (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps one fixed wording for every line of the list (verses 5-49), as in 21:10-11, so that the reader hears the repetition of the Hebrew.

source.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִסֻּכֹּ֑ת וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְאֵתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, which [is] on [the] edge of the wilderness.

en.L: And they set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, which [is] at the edge of the wilderness.
en.B: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
en.R: They left Succoth and camped at Etham, where the desert begins.

es.L: Y partieron de Sucot y acamparon en Etam, que [está] en el extremo del desierto.
es.B: Partieron de Sucot y acamparon en Etam, al borde del desierto.
es.R: Salieron de Sucot y acamparon en Etam, donde comienza el desierto.

fr.L: Et ils partirent de Souccoth et campèrent à Étham, qui [est] à l’extrémité du désert.
fr.B: Ils partirent de Souccoth et campèrent à Étham, en bordure du désert.
fr.R: Ils ont quitté Souccoth et ont campé à Étham, là où commence le désert.

sw.L: Nao wakasafiri kutoka Sukothi, wakapiga kambi Ethamu, iliyo ukingoni mwa nyika.
sw.B: Walisafiri kutoka Sukothi, wakapiga kambi Ethamu, ukingoni mwa nyika.
sw.R: Waliondoka Sukothi, wakapiga kambi Ethamu, mahali jangwa linapoanzia.

decisions.choice: Etham, at the edge of the wilderness
decisions.reason: Etham is the second camp in Exodus 13:20, where the settled land ended and the desert began. Its site is not known.

source.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽאֵתָ֔ם וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ עַל־פִּ֣י הַחִירֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־פְּנֵ֖י בַּ֣עַל צְפ֑וֹן וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י מִגְדֹּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which [is] on [the] face of Baal-zephon, and they camped before Migdol.

en.L: And they set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which [is] facing Baal-zephon, and they camped before Migdol.
en.B: They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and they camped in front of Migdol.
en.R: They left Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, across from Baal-zephon, and they camped near Migdol.

es.L: Y partieron de Etam y volvieron hacia Pi-hahirot, que [está] frente a Baal-zefón, y acamparon delante de Migdol.
es.B: Partieron de Etam y se volvieron hacia Pi-hahirot, que está frente a Baal-zefón, y acamparon delante de Migdol.
es.R: Salieron de Etam y dieron la vuelta hacia Pi-hahirot, frente a Baal-zefón, y acamparon cerca de Migdol.

fr.L: Et ils partirent d’Étham et retournèrent vers Pi-Hahiroth, qui [est] en face de Baal-Tsephôn, et ils campèrent devant Migdol.
fr.B: Ils partirent d’Étham et revinrent sur leurs pas vers Pi-Hahiroth, qui fait face à Baal-Tsephôn, et ils campèrent devant Migdol.
fr.R: Ils ont quitté Étham et ont fait demi-tour vers Pi-Hahiroth, en face de Baal-Tsephôn, et ils ont campé près de Migdol.

sw.L: Nao wakasafiri kutoka Ethamu, wakarudi nyuma mpaka Pi-hahirothi, iliyo mbele ya Baal-sefoni, wakapiga kambi mbele ya Migdoli.
sw.B: Walisafiri kutoka Ethamu, wakarudi nyuma hadi Pi-hahirothi, inayoelekeana na Baal-sefoni, wakapiga kambi mbele ya Migdoli.
sw.R: Waliondoka Ethamu, wakageuka kurudi Pi-hahirothi, mkabala na Baal-sefoni, wakapiga kambi karibu na Migdoli.

decisions.choice: turned back: the turn God ordered before the crossing of the sea
decisions.reason: Exodus 14:2 tells of God's order to turn back and camp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, facing Baal-zephon. None of the three places can be located with certainty today.

decisions.choice: he turned back: the whole people spoken of as one
decisions.reason: The verb "turned back" is singular, between plural verbs. The people are spoken of as one body for this single move; the sense is that they all turned back.

source.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הַֽחִירֹ֔ת וַיַּֽעַבְר֥וּ בְתוֹךְ־הַיָּ֖ם הַמִּדְבָּ֑רָה וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ דֶּ֣רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר אֵתָ֔ם וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out from before Hahiroth and passed through [the] midst of the sea into the wilderness, and they went [a] journey of three days in [the] wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.

en.L: And they set out from before Hahiroth and passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness, and they went a journey of three days in the wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
en.B: They set out from Pi-hahiroth and went through the middle of the sea into the wilderness. After three days' travel in the wilderness of Etham, they camped at Marah.
en.R: They left Pi-hahiroth and walked through the middle of the sea into the desert. They traveled for three days in the Desert of Etham and camped at Marah.

es.L: Y partieron de delante de Hahirot y pasaron por en medio del mar hacia el desierto; y anduvieron camino de tres días por el desierto de Etam y acamparon en Mara.
es.B: Partieron de Pi-hahirot y cruzaron por en medio del mar hasta el desierto. Después de tres días de camino por el desierto de Etam, acamparon en Mara.
es.R: Salieron de Pi-hahirot y caminaron por en medio del mar hasta el desierto. Anduvieron tres días por el desierto de Etam y acamparon en Mara.

fr.L: Et ils partirent de devant Hahiroth et passèrent au milieu de la mer vers le désert ; et ils firent une marche de trois jours dans le désert d’Étham et campèrent à Mara.
fr.B: Ils partirent de Pi-Hahiroth et traversèrent la mer par le milieu pour gagner le désert. Après trois jours de marche dans le désert d’Étham, ils campèrent à Mara.
fr.R: Ils ont quitté Pi-Hahiroth et ont marché au milieu de la mer jusqu’au désert. Ils ont marché pendant trois jours dans le désert d’Étham et ils ont campé à Mara.

sw.L: Nao wakasafiri kutoka mbele ya Hahirothi, wakapita katikati ya bahari kuingia nyikani, wakaenda mwendo wa siku tatu katika nyika ya Ethamu, wakapiga kambi Mara.
sw.B: Walisafiri kutoka Pi-hahirothi, wakapita katikati ya bahari kuingia nyikani. Baada ya mwendo wa siku tatu katika nyika ya Ethamu, wakapiga kambi Mara.
sw.R: Waliondoka Pi-hahirothi, wakatembea katikati ya bahari mpaka jangwani. Walitembea siku tatu katika jangwa la Ethamu, wakapiga kambi Mara.

decisions.choice: Hahiroth: a shorter form of Pi-hahiroth
decisions.reason: The name lacks its first part here. It is the same place as in verse 7, and "from before" means from the camp in front of it.

decisions.choice: passed through the midst of the sea: the crossing of Exodus 14
decisions.reason: The great rescue of Exodus 14:21-29 is told here in a single clause. The list keeps to the stages of the route.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Etham and Marah
decisions.reason: The desert east of the sea is called the wilderness of Shur in Exodus 15:22, and here the wilderness of Etham, after the camp of verse 6. Marah, "bitter", was named for its bitter water (Exodus 15:23).

decisions.choice: Pi-hahiroth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the full name used in verse 7, so that the reader can see it is the same place. Literal keeps the shorter form.

source.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִמָּרָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֵילִ֑מָה וּ֠בְאֵילִם שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֞ה עֵינֹ֥ת מַ֛יִם וְשִׁבְעִ֥ים תְּמָרִ֖ים וַיַּחֲנוּ־שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out from Marah and came to Elim; and at Elim [were] twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.

en.L: And they set out from Marah and came to Elim; and at Elim [were] twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
en.B: They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
en.R: They left Marah and came to Elim. There were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees at Elim, so they camped there.

es.L: Y partieron de Mara y llegaron a Elim; y en Elim [había] doce fuentes de agua y setenta palmeras, y acamparon allí.
es.B: Partieron de Mara y llegaron a Elim, donde había doce fuentes de agua y setenta palmeras, y acamparon allí.
es.R: Salieron de Mara y llegaron a Elim. En Elim había doce manantiales y setenta palmeras, así que acamparon allí.

fr.L: Et ils partirent de Mara et arrivèrent à Élim ; et à Élim [il y avait] douze sources d’eau et soixante-dix palmiers, et ils campèrent là.
fr.B: Ils partirent de Mara et arrivèrent à Élim, où il y avait douze sources d’eau et soixante-dix palmiers, et ils y campèrent.
fr.R: Ils ont quitté Mara et sont arrivés à Élim. Il y avait à Élim douze sources d’eau et soixante-dix palmiers, alors ils ont campé là.

sw.L: Nao wakasafiri kutoka Mara, wakafika Elimu; na huko Elimu [kulikuwa na] chemchemi kumi na mbili za maji na mitende sabini, wakapiga kambi huko.
sw.B: Walisafiri kutoka Mara, wakafika Elimu, mahali palipokuwa na chemchemi kumi na mbili za maji na mitende sabini, wakapiga kambi huko.
sw.R: Waliondoka Mara, wakafika Elimu. Huko Elimu kulikuwa na chemchemi kumi na mbili za maji na mitende sabini, kwa hiyo wakapiga kambi huko.

decisions.choice: Elim: an oasis after the bitter water of Marah
decisions.reason: Exodus 15:27 tells of the same springs and palm trees. The line breaks the list's pattern ("came to" before "camped") to remember the place where water was plentiful.

decisions.choice: so
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the water and shade are why they camped there, as the order of the Hebrew implies.

sw.R: Waliondoka Elimu, wakapiga kambi kando ya Bahari ya Shamu.

decisions.choice: a camp by the sea between Elim and the wilderness of Sin
decisions.reason: Exodus 16:1 goes straight from Elim to the wilderness of Sin; this camp is named only here. "Sea of Reeds" is the name of the sea of the crossing, but it is also used for the gulfs on either side of the Sinai peninsula (21:4). Here it probably names the western gulf, along which the route ran.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: As in 21:4: Balanced and Readable use the familiar name; Literal translates the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds".

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Sin: where the manna was first given
decisions.reason: Israel reached the wilderness of Sin a month after leaving Egypt, and there the LORD sent quail and manna (Exodus 16:1-15).

decisions.choice: the Desert of Sin
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 16:1, Readable says "desert" for "wilderness" in a place name.

decisions.choice: Dophkah: a camp named only in this list
decisions.reason: Dophkah and Alush (verse 13) stand between the wilderness of Sin and Rephidim, where Exodus 17:1 says only that Israel moved "by their stages". Their sites are not known.

decisions.choice: Dofca, Alús, Ritma, Ceelata, Macelot ...
decisions.reason: Camps named only in this list take the forms long used in Spanish Bibles, which write c for k and drop the doubled consonants and the final h (Ritma, Risa, Mitca).

decisions.choice: Dophka, Aloush, Rithma, Tsalmona, Pounon ...
decisions.reason: Camps named only in this list have no settled French form. They are transcribed from the Hebrew as other minor names in this translation are: "ts" for tsade (Rimmon-Pérets, Tsalmona), "sh" for shin (Hashmona, Shépher), "ou" for the u vowel (Aloush, Pounon), J for yod (Jotbatha), with French accents where French writes them.

decisions.choice: Dofka, Alushi, Rimoni-peresi, Salmona ...
decisions.reason: Camps named only in this list are transcribed from the Hebrew as other names in this translation are: a final vowel where the name ends in a consonant (Alushi, Punoni) and s for tsade (Rimoni-peresi, Salmona).

en.R: They left Alush and camped at Rephidim. There was no water there for the people to drink.

es.R: Salieron de Alús y acamparon en Refidim. Allí el pueblo no tenía agua para beber.

fr.R: Ils ont quitté Aloush et ont campé à Rephidim. Là, le peuple n’avait pas d’eau à boire.

sw.B: Walisafiri kutoka Alushi, wakapiga kambi Refidimu, mahali ambapo hapakuwa na maji ya kunywa kwa ajili ya watu.
sw.R: Waliondoka Alushi, wakapiga kambi Refidimu. Huko watu hawakuwa na maji ya kunywa.

decisions.choice: Rephidim, where there was no water
decisions.reason: Exodus 17:1-7 tells how the people quarreled with Moses there and the LORD gave them water from the rock. The place was named Massah and Meribah. The list recalls only the lack of water.

decisions.reason: Israel camped before the mountain in the third month (Exodus 19:1-2) and stayed there almost a year, until the cloud lifted in the second month of the second year (10:11-12).

How these stops fit the story is not said.

records.literal_gloss: And went up Aaron the priest to Hor the mountain at [the] mouth of Yahweh and died there, in [the] year the fortieth of [the] going out of [the] sons of Israel from [the] land of Egypt, in the month the fifth, on [the] one of the month.

en.L: And Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and died there, in the fortieth year after the going out of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first [day] of the month.
en.B: Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command, and he died there on the first day of the fifth month, in the fortieth year after the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came out of the land of Egypt.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Aaron the priest to go up Mount Hor, and Aaron died there. It was the first day of the fifth month of the fortieth year since the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came out of Egypt.

es.L: Y subió Aarón el sacerdote al monte Hor por boca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y murió allí, en el año cuarenta de la salida de los hijos de Israel de la tierra de Egipto, en el mes quinto, el [día] primero del mes.
es.B: Aarón el sacerdote subió al monte Hor por orden {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y murió allí el primer día del quinto mes, en el año cuarenta después de que los israelitas salieron de la tierra de Egipto.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo al sacerdote Aarón que subiera al monte Hor, y Aarón murió allí. Fue el primer día del quinto mes del año cuarenta desde que los israelitas salieron de Egipto.

fr.L: Et Aaron le prêtre monta sur le mont Hor selon la bouche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et il mourut là, la quarantième année après la sortie des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël du pays d’Égypte, au cinquième mois, le premier [jour] du mois.
fr.B: Aaron le prêtre monta sur le mont Hor sur l’ordre {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et il y mourut le premier jour du cinquième mois, la quarantième année après que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} furent sortis du pays d’Égypte.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit au prêtre Aaron de monter sur le mont Hor, et Aaron est mort là. C’était le premier jour du cinquième mois de la quarantième année depuis que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} étaient sortis d’Égypte.

sw.L: Naye Haruni kuhani akapanda Mlima Hori kwa kinywa cha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akafa huko, katika mwaka wa arobaini tangu kutoka kwa wana wa Israeli katika nchi ya Misri, katika mwezi wa tano, [siku] ya kwanza ya mwezi.
sw.B: Haruni kuhani alipanda Mlima Hori kwa amri ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akafa huko siku ya kwanza ya mwezi wa tano, katika mwaka wa arobaini tangu Waisraeli walipotoka katika nchi ya Misri.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Haruni kuhani apande Mlima Hori, na Haruni akafa huko. Ilikuwa siku ya kwanza ya mwezi wa tano katika mwaka wa arobaini tangu Waisraeli walipotoka Misri.

decisions.choice: Aaron's death on Mount Hor
decisions.reason: The full account is in 20:22-29: Aaron went up the mountain with Moses and his son Eleazar, his priestly garments were put on Eleazar, and he died there. The list breaks off to remember him.

decisions.choice: the first day of the fifth month of the fortieth year
decisions.reason: Only here is the date of Aaron's death given. It places the end of the wilderness years: Israel left Egypt in the first month of the first year (verse 3), so almost forty years had passed.

decisions.choice: at the mouth of Yahweh: at Yahweh's command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what is spoken, as in verse 2. Aaron went up because the LORD told him to (20:23-26).

decisions.choice: told Aaron ... to go up
decisions.reason: Readable turns "at the LORD's command" into a clause of its own, which says the same thing in plainer words.

decisions.choice: 123 years: in line with the age given at the exodus
decisions.reason: Aaron was 83 when he and Moses spoke to Pharaoh (Exodus 7:7). Forty years later he was 123. Moses died at 120 (Deuteronomy 34:7).

en.R: The Canaanite king of Arad lived in the Negev, the dry country in the south of Canaan. He heard that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} were coming.

es.B: El rey cananeo de Arad, que vivía en el Néguev, en la tierra de Canaán, se enteró de que los israelitas venían.
es.R: El rey cananeo de Arad vivía en el Néguev, la región seca del sur de Canaán. Supo que los israelitas venían.

fr.L: Et le Cananéen, le roi d’Arad, qui habitait dans le Néguev, au pays de Canaan, apprit la venue des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël.
fr.B: Le roi cananéen d’Arad, qui habitait le Néguev, au pays de Canaan, apprit que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} arrivaient.
fr.R: Le roi cananéen d’Arad vivait dans le Néguev, la région sèche au sud de Canaan. Il a appris que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} arrivaient.

sw.L: Naye Mkanaani, mfalme wa Aradi, aliyekuwa akikaa Negebu katika nchi ya Kanaani, akasikia habari za kuja kwa wana wa Israeli.
sw.B: Mfalme Mkanaani wa Aradi, aliyeishi Negebu katika nchi ya Kanaani, alisikia kwamba Waisraeli walikuwa wakija.
sw.R: Mfalme Mkanaani wa Aradi aliishi Negebu, nchi kavu ya kusini mwa Kanaani. Alisikia kwamba Waisraeli walikuwa wakija.

decisions.choice: the king of Arad: the attack and defeat of 21:1-3
decisions.reason: The full story is in 21:1-3: the king attacked Israel, and Israel vowed to devote his towns to destruction and did so. The list recalls only that he heard Israel was coming, which places the event at this stage of the route.

decisions.choice: the Negev: the dry southern part of Canaan
decisions.reason: The word means the dry land and also "the south". It names the desert country in the south of Canaan, where Arad lay.

decisions.choice: the dry country in the south of
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name Negev, as at 21:1.

decisions.reason: Dibon was a town of Moab taken by Israel (21:30). It is called Dibon-gad because the tribe of Gad rebuilt it (32:34).

decisions.choice: Iye-abarim
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the full name used in verse 44, so that the reader can see it is the same place. Literal keeps the shorter form.

decisions.choice: the mountains of the Abarim, facing Nebo
decisions.reason: Abarim, "the regions beyond", is the range of hills east of the Dead Sea. Nebo is one of its heights, from which Moses would see the land and where he died (27:12; Deuteronomy 32:49; 34:1).

decisions.choice: Mount Nebo
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Mount" to show that Nebo is one of the heights, as Deuteronomy 32:49 calls it.

source.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵהָרֵ֣י הָעֲבָרִ֑ים וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בְּעַֽרְבֹ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב עַ֖ל יַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרֵחֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out from the mountains of the Abarim and camped in [the] plains of Moab by [the] Jordan [of] Jericho.

en.B: They set out from the Abarim mountains and camped in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan, across from Jericho.
en.R: They left the Abarim Mountains and camped on the flat land of Moab, beside the Jordan River across from Jericho.

es.L: Y partieron de los montes de Abarim y acamparon en las llanuras de Moab, junto al Jordán, [frente a] Jericó.
es.B: Partieron de los montes Abarim y acamparon en las llanuras de Moab, junto al Jordán, frente a Jericó.
es.R: Salieron de los montes Abarim y acamparon en la llanura de Moab, junto al río Jordán, frente a Jericó.

fr.L: Et ils partirent des montagnes des Abarim et campèrent dans les plaines de Moab, près du Jourdain, [en face de] Jéricho.
fr.B: Ils partirent des monts Abarim et campèrent dans les plaines de Moab, au bord du Jourdain, en face de Jéricho.
fr.R: Ils ont quitté les monts Abarim et ont campé dans la plaine de Moab, au bord du fleuve Jourdain, en face de Jéricho.

sw.L: Nao wakasafiri kutoka milima ya Abarimu, wakapiga kambi katika nchi tambarare za Moabu, kando ya Yordani [mkabala na] Yeriko.
sw.B: Walisafiri kutoka milima ya Abarimu, wakapiga kambi katika nchi tambarare za Moabu, kando ya Yordani, mkabala na Yeriko.
sw.R: Waliondoka milima ya Abarimu, wakapiga kambi katika nchi tambarare ya Moabu, kando ya Mto Yordani, mkabala na Yeriko.

decisions.choice: the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho: the last camp
decisions.reason: The plains are the low land on the east side of the Jordan, opposite Jericho, where Israel camped from 22:1 to the end of the book (36:13). The phrase "the Jordan of Jericho" names the stretch of the river across from that city.

decisions.choice: across from Jericho
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where Jericho lay, on the other bank, as in 22:1. Literal brackets "at".

source.text: וַיַּחֲנ֤וּ עַל־הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ מִבֵּ֣ית הַיְשִׁמֹ֔ת עַ֖ד אָבֵ֣ל הַשִּׁטִּ֑ים בְּעַֽרְבֹ֖ת מוֹאָֽב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they camped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim in [the] plains of Moab.

en.L: And they camped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab.
en.B: Their camp stretched along the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab.
en.R: Their camp spread out along the Jordan River all the way from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim, on the flat land of Moab.

es.L: Y acamparon junto al Jordán, desde Bet-jesimot hasta Abel-sitim, en las llanuras de Moab.
es.B: Su campamento se extendía a lo largo del Jordán, desde Bet-jesimot hasta Abel-sitim, en las llanuras de Moab.
es.R: Su campamento ocupaba toda la orilla del río Jordán, desde Bet-jesimot hasta Abel-sitim, en la llanura de Moab.

fr.L: Et ils campèrent près du Jourdain, depuis Beth-Jeshimoth jusqu’à Abel-Shittim, dans les plaines de Moab.
fr.B: Leur camp s’étendait le long du Jourdain, de Beth-Jeshimoth à Abel-Shittim, dans les plaines de Moab.
fr.R: Leur camp occupait toute la rive du fleuve Jourdain, depuis Beth-Jeshimoth jusqu’à Abel-Shittim, dans la plaine de Moab.

sw.L: Nao wakapiga kambi kando ya Yordani, kutoka Beth-yeshimothi mpaka Abel-shitimu, katika nchi tambarare za Moabu.
sw.B: Kambi yao ilienea kando ya Yordani, kutoka Beth-yeshimothi hadi Abel-shitimu, katika nchi tambarare za Moabu.
sw.R: Kambi yao ilienea kote kando ya Mto Yordani, tangu Beth-yeshimothi mpaka Abel-shitimu, katika nchi tambarare ya Moabu.

decisions.choice: from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim: the length of the camp
decisions.reason: The two names mark the ends of the camp along the river. Abel-shittim, "meadow of acacias", is the Shittim of 25:1, from which Joshua later sent the spies (Joshua 2:1). Beth-jeshimoth lay nearer the Dead Sea (Joshua 12:3).

decisions.choice: they camped: the list ends without a further setting out
decisions.reason: This line has "camped" but no "set out". The journey stops here, where Israel stays until it crosses the Jordan (Joshua 3:1).

decisions.choice: Their camp stretched / spread out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that "camped from ... as far as ..." describes the extent of the camp, not one more move.

decisions.choice: a new section: laws for entering the land
decisions.reason: With the journey over, the LORD speaks to Moses at the last camp. The commands from here to the end of the book (chapters 33-36) all look ahead to life in Canaan and are given at this place (36:13).

decisions.choice: across from Jericho
decisions.reason: As in verse 48.

source.text: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כִּ֥י אַתֶּ֛ם עֹבְרִ֥ים אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃

en.L: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, 'When you cross over the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
en.B: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
en.R: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'You are going to cross the Jordan River into the land of Canaan.

fr.B: « Parle aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} et dis-leur : “Lorsque vous aurez traversé le Jourdain pour entrer dans le pays de Canaan,

decisions.choice: when you cross: an event close at hand
decisions.reason: The verb form describes the crossing as about to happen. The clause sets the time for the commands in verses 52-56.

decisions.choice: You are going to cross ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes the time clause a sentence of its own and picks it up at the start of verse 52 with "When you do".

records.literal_gloss: then you will drive out all [the] inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their figured [stones], and all [the] images of their cast [metal] you will destroy, and all their high places you will demolish.

en.L: then you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their carved stones, and all their cast images you shall destroy, and all their high places you shall demolish.
en.B: drive out all the people who live in the land ahead of you. Destroy all their carved stones, destroy all their cast metal idols, and tear down all their high places.
en.R: When you do, force out all the people who live there. Destroy all their stone idols and their metal idols, and tear down all their hilltop shrines.

es.B: {{plural_you:expulsen|expulsad}} de delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a todos los habitantes de la tierra. {{plural_you:Destruyan|Destruid}} todas sus piedras esculpidas, {{plural_you:destruyan|destruid}} todos sus ídolos de metal fundido y {{plural_you:derriben|derribad}} todos sus lugares altos.
es.R: Cuando lo {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}}, {{plural_you:echen|echad}} a toda la gente que vive allí. {{plural_you:Destruyan|Destruid}} todos sus ídolos de piedra y de metal, y {{plural_you:derriben|derribad}} todos sus santuarios de las colinas.

fr.L: alors vous chasserez de devant vous tous les habitants du pays, et vous détruirez toutes leurs pierres sculptées, et toutes leurs images de métal fondu, vous [les] détruirez, et tous leurs hauts lieux, vous [les] démolirez.
fr.B: chassez devant vous tous les habitants du pays. Détruisez toutes leurs pierres sculptées, détruisez toutes leurs idoles de métal fondu et démolissez tous leurs hauts lieux.
fr.R: Quand vous l’aurez traversé, chassez tous les gens qui habitent là. Détruisez toutes leurs idoles de pierre et de métal, et démolissez tous leurs sanctuaires des collines.

sw.R: Mtakapofanya hivyo, wafukuzeni watu wote wanaoishi huko. Haribuni sanamu zao zote za mawe na za madini, na bomoeni mahali pao pote pa ibada vilimani.

decisions.choice: drive out: take away the land from its people
decisions.reason: The verb means to dispossess: to make the people of the land leave so that Israel may hold it. The same root comes again in verse 53, "take possession".

decisions.choice: their carved stones: stones carved with images for worship
decisions.reason: The word names a stone with figures cut into it. Leviticus 26:1 forbids Israel to set one up and bow down to it.

decisions.choice: their cast images: idols made of molten metal
decisions.reason: These are images made by pouring melted metal into a mold, like the calf of Exodus 32:4.

decisions.choice: their high places: places of worship, often on raised ground
decisions.reason: A high place was an open-air shrine, often on a hill, with an altar and other objects of worship (Leviticus 26:30).

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: Readable says what a high place was. Literal and Balanced keep "high places".

source.text: וְהוֹרַשְׁתֶּ֥ם אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ וִֽישַׁבְתֶּם־בָּ֑הּ כִּ֥י לָכֶ֛ם נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ לָרֶ֥שֶׁת אֹתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take possession of the land and dwell in it, for to you I have given the land to possess it.

en.L: And you shall take possession of the land and live in it, for to you I have given the land, to possess it.
en.B: Take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given the land to you to possess.
en.R: Take the land for your own and live in it. I have given it to you to be yours.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:tomarán|tomaréis}} posesión de la tierra y {{plural_you:habitarán|habitaréis}} en ella, porque a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado la tierra, para que la {{plural_you:posean|poseáis}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} posesión de la tierra y {{plural_you:establézcanse|estableceos}} en ella, porque yo {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado la tierra para que la {{plural_you:posean|poseáis}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} la tierra para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:vivan|vivid}} en ella. Yo {{plural_you:se la|os la}} he dado para que sea {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}.

fr.L: Et vous prendrez possession du pays et vous y habiterez, car c’est à vous que j’ai donné le pays, pour le posséder.
fr.B: Prenez possession du pays et habitez-y, car je vous ai donné ce pays pour que vous le possédiez.
fr.R: Prenez le pays pour vous et vivez-y. Je vous l’ai donné, il est à vous.

sw.L: Nanyi mtaimiliki nchi na kukaa ndani yake, kwa maana ninyi nimewapa nchi, ili kuimiliki.
sw.B: Imilikini nchi na kukaa ndani yake, kwa kuwa nimewapa nchi hiyo muimiliki.
sw.R: Ichukueni nchi iwe yenu, mkaishi ndani yake. Nimewapa ninyi, iwe mali yenu.

decisions.choice: take possession: hold the land as your own
decisions.reason: The verb is from the same root as "drive out" in verse 52. Driving out the nations and taking hold of the land are two sides of one act.

decisions.choice: I have given the land: Israel's claim rests on God's gift
decisions.reason: The land is Israel's because the LORD gives it (Exodus 6:8). It remains his, and Israel holds it under him (Leviticus 25:23).

decisions.choice: to you I have given
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "to you" first, as the Hebrew puts it for emphasis. Balanced and Readable use normal English order.

source.text: וְהִתְנַחַלְתֶּם֩ אֶת־הָאָ֨רֶץ בְּגוֹרָ֜ל לְמִשְׁפְּחֹֽתֵיכֶ֗ם לָרַ֞ב תַּרְבּ֤וּ אֶת־נַחֲלָתוֹ֙ וְלַמְעַט֙ תַּמְעִ֣יט אֶת־נַחֲלָת֔וֹ אֶל֩ אֲשֶׁר־יֵ֨צֵא ל֥וֹ שָׁ֛מָּה הַגּוֹרָ֖ל ל֣וֹ יִהְיֶ֑ה לְמַטּ֥וֹת אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם תִּתְנֶחָֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will inherit the land by lot by your clans; to the many you will make great his inheritance, and to the few you will make small his inheritance; to where goes out for him there the lot, to him it will be; by [the] tribes of your fathers you will inherit.

en.L: And you shall take the land as an inheritance by lot according to your clans: to the larger you shall make its inheritance larger, and to the smaller you shall make its inheritance smaller. Wherever the lot goes out for it, there it shall be its [own]. By the tribes of your fathers you shall take your inheritance.
en.B: Divide the land among yourselves as an inheritance by lot, clan by clan. Give a larger inheritance to a larger clan and a smaller inheritance to a smaller one. Wherever the lot falls for a clan, that place will be its own. You are to receive your inheritance by your ancestral tribes.
en.R: Divide the land by drawing lots, clan by clan. Give more land to the larger clans and less land to the smaller ones. Each clan will get the place where its lot falls. Divide the land by the tribes of your ancestors.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:heredarán|heredaréis}} la tierra por suerte según {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} clanes: al mayor le {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} mayor su herencia, y al menor le {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} menor su herencia. Donde le salga la suerte, allí será [lo] suyo. Según las tribus de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} padres {{plural_you:heredarán|heredaréis}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Repártanse|Repartíos}} la tierra como herencia por sorteo, clan por clan. A un clan grande {{plural_you:denle|dadle}} una herencia mayor, y a uno pequeño, una herencia menor. Donde le caiga la suerte a un clan, ese lugar será suyo. {{plural_you:Recibirán|Recibiréis}} {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} herencia según las tribus de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} antepasados.
es.R: {{plural_you:Repartan|Repartid}} la tierra echando suertes, clan por clan. {{plural_you:Den|Dad}} más tierra a los clanes grandes y menos tierra a los pequeños. Cada clan recibirá el lugar donde le toque la suerte. {{plural_you:Repartan|Repartid}} la tierra según las tribus de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} antepasados.

fr.L: Et vous recevrez le pays en héritage par le sort, selon vos clans : au plus grand vous ferez un héritage plus grand, et au plus petit vous ferez un héritage plus petit. Là où le sort sortira pour lui, là sera [sa part]. Selon les tribus de vos pères vous recevrez votre héritage.
fr.B: Partagez-vous le pays en héritage par tirage au sort, clan par clan. Donnez un héritage plus grand à un clan plus nombreux et un héritage plus petit à un clan moins nombreux. Là où le sort tombera pour un clan, cet endroit sera à lui. C’est selon les tribus de vos ancêtres que vous recevrez votre héritage.
fr.R: Partagez le pays en tirant au sort, clan par clan. Donnez plus de terre aux grands clans et moins de terre aux petits. Chaque clan recevra l’endroit où son sort sera tombé. Partagez le pays selon les tribus de vos ancêtres.

sw.L: Nanyi mtairithi nchi kwa kura kwa koo zenu: kwa [ukoo] mkubwa mtauongeza urithi wake, na kwa mdogo mtaupunguza urithi wake. Popote kura itakapoutokea, hapo patakuwa pake. Kwa makabila ya baba zenu mtarithi.
sw.B: Gawanyeni nchi kati yenu kuwa urithi kwa kura, ukoo kwa ukoo. Ukoo mkubwa mpeni urithi mkubwa zaidi, na ukoo mdogo mpeni urithi mdogo zaidi. Popote kura itakapouangukia ukoo, mahali hapo patakuwa pake. Mtapokea urithi wenu kufuatana na makabila ya mababu zenu.
sw.R: Gawanyeni nchi kwa kupiga kura, ukoo kwa ukoo. Zipeni koo kubwa nchi zaidi, na koo ndogo nchi kidogo. Kila ukoo utapata mahali ambapo kura yake itaangukia. Gawanyeni nchi kufuatana na makabila ya mababu zenu.

decisions.choice: take as an inheritance: divide among yourselves as lasting family property
decisions.reason: The verb form means to receive an inheritance for oneself, here by sharing out the land among the clans. An inheritance was property that stayed in the family.

decisions.choice: the lot and the size of the clan
decisions.reason: The same rule is given in 26:52-56. The lot decided where each group's land lay; the size of the group decided how much land it received.

decisions.choice: his inheritance, for him, to him: each clan
decisions.reason: The pronouns are singular and refer to each clan (or group) that receives a share, not to one man.

decisions.choice: its / a clan / each clan
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "him" and "his" for the clan, as grammar requires. Each level says "it" or names the clan, since English uses "it" for a group.

decisions.choice: ancestral tribes / tribes of your ancestors
decisions.reason: "The tribes of your fathers" are the tribes named for Israel's ancestors. Literal keeps "fathers".

source.text: וְאִם־לֹ֨א תוֹרִ֜ישׁוּ אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָרֶץ֮ מִפְּנֵיכֶם֒ וְהָיָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תּוֹתִ֣ירוּ מֵהֶ֔ם לְשִׂכִּים֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וְלִצְנִינִ֖ם בְּצִדֵּיכֶ֑ם וְצָרֲר֣וּ אֶתְכֶ֔ם עַל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם יֹשְׁבִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if not you drive out [the] inhabitants of the land from before you, then will be [those] whom you leave of them as barbs in your eyes and as thorns in your sides, and they will harass you in the land in which you [are] dwelling.

en.L: But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those of them whom you let remain shall be as barbs in your eyes and as thorns in your sides, and they shall harass you in the land in which you are living.
en.B: But if you do not drive out the people who live in the land ahead of you, those you allow to stay will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They will make trouble for you in the land where you live.
en.R: But suppose you do not force out the people who live there. Then the ones you let stay will hurt you like a stick in your eye or a thorn in your side. They will cause you trouble in the land where you live.

es.L: Pero si no {{plural_you:expulsan|expulsáis}} de delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a los habitantes de la tierra, entonces los que {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} de ellos serán como púas en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} ojos y como espinas en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} costados, y {{plural_you:los|os}} hostigarán en la tierra en que {{plural_you:habitan|habitáis}}.
es.B: Pero si no {{plural_you:expulsan|expulsáis}} de delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a los habitantes de la tierra, los que {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} quedarse serán como astillas en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} ojos y espinas en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} costados. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} causarán problemas en la tierra donde {{plural_you:viven|vivís}}.
es.R: Pero supongamos que no {{plural_you:echan|echáis}} a la gente que vive allí. Entonces los que {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} quedarse {{plural_you:les|os}} harán daño, como una astilla en el ojo o una espina en el costado. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} causarán problemas en la tierra donde {{plural_you:viven|vivís}}.

fr.L: Mais si vous ne chassez pas de devant vous les habitants du pays, alors ceux d’entre eux que vous laisserez seront comme des pointes dans vos yeux et comme des épines dans vos flancs, et ils vous harcèleront dans le pays où vous habitez.
fr.B: Mais si vous ne chassez pas devant vous les habitants du pays, ceux que vous laisserez rester seront comme des échardes dans vos yeux et des épines dans vos flancs. Ils vous causeront des ennuis dans le pays où vous habitez.
fr.R: Mais imaginez que vous ne chassiez pas les gens qui habitent là. Alors ceux que vous laisserez rester vous feront mal, comme une écharde dans l’œil ou une épine dans le côté. Ils vous causeront des problèmes dans le pays où vous vivez.

sw.L: Lakini kama hamtawafukuza wakazi wa nchi mbele yenu, ndipo wale mtakaowaacha miongoni mwao watakuwa kama vibanzi machoni mwenu na kama miiba mbavuni mwenu, nao watawasumbua katika nchi mnayoikaa.
sw.B: Lakini msipowafukuza wakazi wa nchi mbele yenu, wale mtakaowaacha wabaki watakuwa kama vibanzi machoni mwenu na miiba mbavuni mwenu. Watawaletea taabu katika nchi mnayoishi.
sw.R: Lakini tuseme hamtawafukuza watu wanaoishi huko. Basi wale mtakaowaacha wabaki watawaumiza kama kijiti jichoni au mwiba ubavuni. Watawaletea matatizo katika nchi mnayoishi.

decisions.choice: barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides: a constant source of pain
decisions.reason: Something sharp in the eye or the side never lets a person rest. The people left in the land would trouble Israel without end. Joshua 23:13 and Judges 2:3 take up the same picture.

decisions.choice: harass: press hard and act as an enemy
decisions.reason: The verb means to show hostility, to put someone in distress. The danger is both conflict and the pull of their worship (Exodus 23:33).

decisions.choice: But suppose you do not force out ... Then ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits the condition and its result into two sentences.

decisions.choice: a warning: Israel would face what the nations faced
decisions.reason: The LORD planned to remove the nations from the land for their wrongs (Leviticus 18:24-25). If Israel let them stay and followed their ways, Israel too would lose the land (Leviticus 18:28; Deuteronomy 28:63).

decisions.choice: intended: planned, set in mind
decisions.reason: The verb means to think out or plan. What God planned for the nations he could also carry out against his own people.
